sourceInformation.source: Solaris (1986), Atari 2600 game by Doug Neubauer
sourceInformation.genre: Arcade space shooter, rescue, and sector strategy
sourceInformation.perspective: Third-person chase camera and strategic sector chart
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPU renderer with WebGL2 compatibility, Rapier 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API, WebRTC, AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Stylized cel shading, dark ink outlines, faceted spacecraft, amber and mint frontier palette
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip, and keyframe tracks; procedural steering and particles
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated synthesizer music (10% default), synthesized effects, Animalese-style formant radio voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 shared-world co-op via AI Hub; standalone WebRTC invitation/reply codes; host-authoritative simulation
sourceInformation.testing: 171 checks: headless Chromium software WebGPU; emulated standard controller and touch; a complete campaign without cheats; offline Web Audio; two-page WebRTC; official AI Hub harness with 150ms latency, 50ms jitter, 5% loss, host departure, and dedicated server. Visual inspection uses WebGL2 captures. No FPS targets.
sourceInformation.research: No internet research; native model knowledge. Retrieved only the explicitly supplied AI Hub integration specification and pinned runtime dependencies.

testingFeedback: Four game defects were caught in executed checks: Rapier reset resource lifetime, an overlapping touch landscape launch panel, a touch pulse button that did not receive taps, and stale render geometry after rapid campaign resets. All were fixed. Test-script formatting errors are excluded.
One was game breaking on touch landscape: the overlapping panel blocked mission launch. It is fixed; no known game-breaking issues remain.
The touch landscape end-to-end check, which found two inaccessible controls. The suite also completes the entire seven-sector campaign without cheats.
Headless WebGPU screenshots: the canvas can be blank despite a working scene. Runtime state checks and WebGL2 compatibility captures were more useful.
engineFeedback: Three.js supports procedural geometry, crisp toon shading, and native animation clips in one scene, with a WebGPU renderer and a compatibility backend.

Entity IDs were initially treated as strings in one animation; review corrected that. Visual inspection also found stale geometry after rapid resets. Headless WebGPU captures were blank, so rendering state and compatibility captures were used.
The campaign and sector rules, controller UI focus, touch assistance, and host-authoritative multiplayer state synchronization.
Keeping physics contacts, renderer lifetimes, input focus, and remote snapshots coherent across resets and screen changes.
none; all changes are game code, with pinned unmodified engine packages.
A built-in controller-focused UI layer that handles menu focus, sliders, and changing input prompts.
promptFeedback: The source, visual style, and controller-first requirements establish a clear identity, while developer tools and attract mode make the demo easier to explore.
The source label does not specify the platform. The Hub guide suggests a four-player stress test even when a game declares a two-player maximum; this game was tested with its supported two seats.
Integrating the complete campaign, synthesized audio, touch and controller UX, and both multiplayer paths into one portable HTML.
Clarify that Hub stress tests should use the game's declared maximum player count, and explicitly name the source platform.

aiHub.name: Solar Flair
aiHub.description: Fly an inked starfighter across a frontier gone quiet. Rescue stranded survivors, recover route signals, and break the siege of Solaris, solo or with a wingmate.
aiHub.controls: WASD / left stick fly; mouse / right stick aim; LMB or Space / R2 fire; Shift / L2 boost; Q / Square pulse; E / Triangle tractor; Esc / Options pause; touch drag with assisted aim and fire.
